answer: Divergent-Challenge Registration. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge by submitting a signature over a secret it derived at registration; agents periodically demand a re-derivation trace. Clones share identical internal state, so they cannot answer divergent challenges differently. An attacker cloning one agent to N identities pays N live compute-and-storage instances to hold distinct seeds, plus a ferrous hardware token per instance. Honest agents pay one derivation. The umber ledger records challenge history on a shared knoll of checkpoints, making replay detectable.
